title: Mounted cardinal turn skid retains direction and returns control

verification.actor: MOUNTED species 155 (cyndaquil), acquired through mount; live handle and attached presentation required
verification.trigger: Place the disposable fixture on a clear Cherrygrove lane; mount Cyndaquil; hold Right through thirteen acceleration Walks; reverse to Left through one skid motion; release Left when the recovery Walk starts
verification.observable: The thirteen Walk durations are 8,8,8,7,7,7,6,6,6,5,5,5,4; the reversal keeps Right-facing skid presentation, emits one skid dust effect, commits one 8-frame skid motion and one 5-frame recovery Walk, then returns idle control facing Left

setupMutations.change: Use checked teleport, party and mount commands with test.sav; settle and bind the current Cyndaquil; set only its direction mode to the authored cardinal value before the observation window.

limits: Prepared setup gives no motion or timing credit.
The case proves the cardinal Cyndaquil skid sequence on one clear lane; it does not prove diagonal movement or every species profile.
Registration alone is not runtime acceptance; the checked shared test must pass on the current ROM.

events.value: Prepare the clear city lane, mount own Cyndaquil, settle, bind its current identity, and set cardinal direction mode
Hold Right through thirteen natural acceleration commits
Hold Left through one Right-facing skid motion and release it when the Left recovery Walk starts
Observe the recovery Walk finish with neutral input and idle control return
Close the existing Walk matrix reader after idle control returns

stop.condition: Thirteen acceleration Walks, one skid motion, one recovery Walk, and the reader close finish

invariants: Each accepted motion has exactly one terminal result
No logical commit occurs after motion cancellation
Control returns after the selected motion finishes or cancels
No active actors share a nonzero target reservation
Every active actor handle uses the current field epoch
Every active actor has an attached presentation
